subject: MAP: Alder Health — success criteria, exit gates, and procurement checkpoints
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhang <claire.zhang@alderhealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Alder Health — success criteria, exit gates, and procurement checkpoints

Claire — great to meet last week. Following up with a draft mutual action plan so we can align on what ‚success’ looks like for Alder’s evaluation and what procurement needs to unblock signature. High level: 6-week technical evaluation (pilot) + 8-week measured production ramp. Key asks below — please confirm/annotate.

Summary of primary acceptance gates (draft):
- Gate 1 (Week 2): Integration & data sanity — live API calls to non-prod dataset, no PII exfiltration, response rate >= 95% for sample set.
- Gate 2 (Week 4): Latency & throughput — 95th percentile latency <= 280ms for 512-token requests under 10rps baseline; sustained handling of 30rps burst for 5 minutes.
- Gate 3 (Week 6): Quality & concordance — accuracy/concordance >= 88% on the clinical extraction prompt set (shared).
- Gate 4 (Onboarding signoff): Operational requirements — audit logs enabled, KMS keys verified, SOC2 summary reviewed.

Exit / fail-fast triggers:
- Any data-security exception reproducing across environments (critical).
- Sustained SLA misses for 48+ hours without remediation plan.

Attachments: initial MAP workbook (Redwood-Alder-MAP-v1.xlsx), SOC2_Summary_2026.pdf, and a short acceptance-tests doc.

Next steps I propose:
1) Claire: confirm internal stakeholders + procurement timelines by EOD Friday 7/16.
2) Alder: mark which Gate is contractually required for payment milestone (if any).
3) Redwood: laura + marcus will publish the acceptance-test cases and test harness by Monday 7/19.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: MAP: Alder Health — success criteria, exit gates, and procurement checkpoints

Claire / Team — looping in acceptance artifacts and clarifications. Quick answers:
- Latency SLA definition: 95th percentile measured at Redwood edge to the model runtime in us-west-2. We'll include a short synthetic test harness that runs from your VPC peering endpoint to validate network delta; documented in Acceptance-Test-Cases.md (attached).
- Clinical prompt set: link in related_links (we uploaded to secure drive). We'll provide both the prompt inputs and expected outputs for concordance scoring; you can run locally.
- Committed spend estimate: $52,000 / month (dedicated baseline for 4x A100 equivalent reserved capacity) — final quote to be in SOW.

Acceptance test highlights (short):
- Security: KMS key rotation validated, audit logs appear within 60s of request, no PII in logs (sample redaction checks).
- Functional: end-to-end extraction pipeline returns expected schema for 95/100 sample documents.
- Performance: p95 <= 280ms for single-session 512-token generation during 10rps baseline.

We'll add a simple checklist to the MAP workbook that ties each Gate to a test owner. Rafael — I assigned Marcus to run the perf harness and myself to own procurement artifacts.

Laura Bennett
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Zhang <claire.zhang@alderhealth.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 11:27:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MAP: Alder Health — success criteria, exit gates, and procurement checkpoints

Claire — quick technical notes and the minimal reproduction steps we'll use for Gate 2 & 3 verification:
1) Perf harness: we'll provide a small k6-based load script that hits the Redwood edge and the model runtime; it reports p50/p95/p99 latency and error rates. Script will include an option to run from your subnet (requires a temporary SSH key / runner).
2) Data sanity tests: provided Python notebook will run 500 sample requests against non-prod dataset and assert schema conformity; failing rows will be flagged in the attached Acceptance-Test-Cases.md.
3) Quality scoring: we'll produce an automated concordance report (F1 + human spot-check) for the 200-sample clinical set. Goal: >= 88% F1; if between 82–88% we enter a remediation sprint (2 weeks) and re-evaluate. Below 82% -> escalation to product/regression path.

Fail modes we'll monitor: tokenization drift with newest model checkpoint (we'll pin model hash for evaluation), and any differing behavior when we switch quantization profile. We'll include model hash, tokenizer version, and quantization profile in the evidence log for each run.

Marcus Lin
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
